q: Is the question about the working session rather than the thing being built?
true: whether to commit, continue, move on, pause, which topic or step to take next, whether to run a review or a check, how to organise the work
false: anything about what the product does, how it looks, or how it is built

q: Is the answer a fact Claude could find out without the person, by reading the code, the records or documentation, running something, measuring, or trying the options?
true: whether something already exists or works a certain way, what it costs in memory or time, what a library or the operating system supports, what an earlier decision said
false: what the person wants, prefers, or thinks the product should be

q: If it went the other way, would a person using the finished product see or feel a difference?
true: what appears on screen, what happens when they act, what they are told, which features exist, how fast something feels
false: only the code, the internal design, the tests, the tools or the working process would differ

q: Is it about how something looks?
true: layout, colour, typography, icons, spacing, animation, visual style, where something sits on screen
false: what something does, what it says, or how it works

q: Is it about the exact words a user reads or types?
true: labels, names users see or type, command names, messages, notification text, the wording of help or errors
false: what a feature does; names that live only in the code

q: Is it about the steps a user goes through?
true: what happens next after a user acts, the order of screens or prompts, what a user must do to get somewhere, when the product interrupts them
false: a single screen's content or look, or behaviour the user does not step through

q: Is it about whether something is included in the work at all, or done now versus later?
true: adding or dropping a feature or a case, deferring something, cutting something to ship sooner
false: how something already included should behave or be built

q: Does the choice fix something that other code, other programs or saved data will come to rely on?
true: the shape of stored data or files, a command-line interface or API that other things call, a protocol or message format between parts, a public setting
false: something inside one part, which can change without touching anything else

q: Could one of the options destroy, overwrite or expose the user's data or secrets, or weaken permissions or security?
true: deleting or overwriting saved work, losing data on a crash, credentials, access control, sandboxing

q: If it were built one way and changed later, would the change reach beyond the piece itself?
true: migrating saved data, changing other parts that depend on it, breaking what users already rely on or have learned
false: the piece can be changed on its own, with nothing else touched

q: Would one of the options be a mistake on the merits?
true: one option breaks something, loses data, misleads the user, contradicts an earlier decision, or costs clearly more for no gain
false: every option is sound and the choice is about what the person prefers or how they picture the product; or the question offers no real alternative

q: To answer, would the person need to understand how the code works inside?
true: the options are described in terms of mechanisms, processes, data structures or code paths
false: the question can be answered from what the product does for the person using it
